correctness.rationale: The exact four-round Hintikka recursion defines T_4 for every chosen ordered four-tuple as its complete equality/strict-between atomic diagram, and T_j as atomic diagram paired with the set of all one-point extension types. An induction gives equivalence with Duplicator winning the remaining game moves; repeated selections are included and the set, not multiset, convention is essential. Independent lossless Python interned all n^4 tuples and all extensions for n=1..17: distinct root types for 1..14 and equal root types at n14..17; n14 and n15 have the same set of one-point types though the center type occurs with different multiplicity. For n>=15, the standard linear-order q4 threshold 2^4-1=15 proves equivalence in the *stronger* oriented order language. The ternary betweenness predicate is quantifier-free in <, so forgetting < preserves q4 equivalence, and transitivity with the finite 14~15 certificate proves the infinite tail. This does not extrapolate from finite n17. The claim is only rank four, strict relation and no additional order constants.

originality.rationale: The familiar 2^q-1 stabilization for oriented finite chains is prior and explicitly invoked. Mwesigye–Truss’s full 11-page 2011 paper was now retrieved through authorized Oxford access and read; it states the ordered-chain character theorem (Theorem 1.2) and standard oriented cutoff, but does not classify this strict betweenness reduct at rank four. Courcelle 2020 treats reconstruction and axioms for betweenness of partial orders, not bounded four-round finite spectra. Published directed successor-only paths and one-red full-order words are different signatures, not direct implications. An earlier folklore result on undirected line betweenness could be equivalent and remains a residual risk.
